svg.text: The Eight Cardinal Movements of Fetal Descent Through the Birth Canal

text.tspan: The biparietal diameter (BPD) of the fetal head
passes through the pelvic inlet. The head enters
in a transverse or oblique position.
The fetal head descends through the pelvic cavity.
This is a continuous process driven by uterine
contractions and maternal pushing efforts.
The chin is brought closer to the chest, presenting
the smaller suboccipitobregmatic diameter (9.5cm)
instead of the larger BPD to ease descent.
The occiput rotates anteriorly from a transverse
position to an anteroposterior position (OA),
aligning with the pelvic outlet shape.
The flexed head extends as it passes under the
symphysis pubis, pivoting on the pubic arch.
The nape of the neck becomes the pivoting point.
After the head is delivered, it rotates back to
realign with the fetal shoulders, undoing the
internal rotation (45° reverse rotation).
The shoulders rotate from transverse to
anteroposterior within the pelvic outlet, allowing
the anterior shoulder to pass under the pubis.
After the shoulders are delivered, the rest of the
fetal body is expelled quickly and easily. The
entire mechanism of labor is now complete.

svg.text: Note: The mechanism of labor describes the positional changes of the fetal head during vertex delivery. Sequential movements are continuous and overlapping.
● Red dot = Occiput marker | Dashed outline = Previous position | Teal arrows = Direction of movement
